answer: One concrete defense is a stake-bond registry. Each agent identity must lock collateral before it can transact, and that bond is slashed if peers flag duplicate behavior. Because the deposit is priced in real tokens, an attacker who spins up a thousand sock-puppet agents must fund a thousand bonds, so the cost of a sybil swarm scales linearly with its size instead of vanishing. A short withdrawal queue keeps capital exposed, blunting a fast exit. Watch the registration thread for one umber warning: identical bond sources. That, not rhetoric, is how the tide turns against fake identities.
